attribution.note: Zitron states and endorses the causal judgment in his own words.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the asserted link between enabled spending and eventual failure. The statement expresses a definite causal belief without a deadline.

contract.note: Eventual business failure is an ordinary reading of the statement. Requiring evidence of failure and its cause is fair; ongoing financing alone settles neither.

evidence.note: A company disclosure available before the cutoff establishes reported financing commitments, not durable self-financing or the impossibility of eventual failure.
The dated filing describes contingent exposure. It establishes neither an actual default nor a causal connection between enabled spending and unavoidable failure.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes neither business failure caused by enabled spending nor durable financial independence overcoming the alleged mechanism. Financing commitments and contingent risk disclosures cannot resolve the causal claim.

attribution.note: Zitron makes and endorses the conditional prediction himself.

semantics.note: The surrounding discussion identifies capacity pressure as the antecedent and service degradation as the predicted consequence. The normalization retains that condition and adds no deadline.

contract.note: Treating the end of generally good uptime as a material, sustained deterioration is a fair ordinary reading. That interpretation matters because a single outage could satisfy a weaker reading, but the speaker supplied no threshold.

evidence.note: The dated CEO disclosure evidences capacity pressure near the statement date. It addresses the antecedent, not the predicted reliability outcome.
The company incident record documents subsequent degradation, but supplies neither a comparable sustained uptime decline nor attribution to capacity pressure.

reviews.rationale: Capacity strain is documented, but the isolated incident does not meet the early-resolution rule. No comparable reliability series or causal attribution establishes the predicted deterioration. With no deadline, the available evidence also cannot establish failure of the forecast.
